main_text.l: plex: alius scilicet est philosophiæ latè, prout à
nobis hîc consideratur, acceptæ, alius philosophiæ

l.i: Intelligimus hîc finé &, cujus nempe gratia res est;
non ω, cui, qui cum subjecto, cui philosophia destinata
est, incidit. Nequetiâ [?] hoc agimus, ut omnes fines, minùs
principales scilicet, accumulemus. Id nobis cordi & cu-
ræ est, ut fines philosophiæ principales (illi enim certi
sunt, & quia certi, brevibus comprehendi præceptis
possunt) colligamus. His enim probè intellectis, fines
illi minùs principales ultrò sese dabunt, utpote qui à
hîc non intelligimus finem executionis, quem vocat Thomas, sed intentionis. Ille enim rectè in effectis, hic in causis numeratur.

main_text.l: Itaq; finis philosophiæ latè acceptæ est in-

ratio ista est perfectio mentis, & orationis.

page.notes: The underlining in the middle of the paragraph beginning "Intelligimus" is a manuscript mark, not printed text, and is not transcribed as print. Greek readings marked [?] are uncertain, as are the Greek symbols in the first margin note and the word "Nequetiâ". The paragraph ends mid-word with "necef-", and the rest is on the next page. The right-hand note "ptor." is the continuation of the note about Thucydides.
